g.text: Precision matters most near the numerical floor

text.style: font-size: 11px; font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; text-anchor: start; fill: #172033

g.text: Same 18 synthetic recordings at each level; same PCM16 input for every variant.

text.style: font-size: 9px; font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; fill: #475569

g.text: Left: nonzero reference maps only (18, 18, 15, 9). A large relative error can represent a tiny absolute change.

text.style: font-size: 9px; font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; fill: #475569

g.text: Right: the dashed blue curve overlaps the original; both already lose nine maps at the weakest level.

text.style: font-size: 9px; font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; fill: #475569

g.text: Nonzero outputs can be quantization artifacts: fewer zero maps does not necessarily mean better quality.

text.style: font-size: 9px; font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; fill: #475569

g.text: These are digital levels, not acoustic SPL. Matching an all-zero reference does not establish detection sensitivity.
